ai.description: This toadfrog reaches 45–60 mm. It features a dark brown dorsum, a white venter with dark mottling, and a distinctive bicolored iris. The skin is smooth with prominent, elongated supratympanic folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Leptobrachium rakhinense* is best distinguished by its distinct bicolored iris, featuring a sharp horizontal division between a dark upper half and a pale lower half.
ai.habitat: *Leptobrachium rakhinense* inhabits evergreen hill forests and rocky streams in the Rakhine Yoma range, typically occurring at elevations between 200 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Rakhine Bicolor-eyed Toadfrog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the forest floor near mountain streams.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Leptobrachium rakhinense* breeds in streams during the monsoon (June–August), laying small clutches of large, unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks or vegetation.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Leptobrachium rakhinense* is found in the Arakan Mountains of Myanmar and potentially adjacent border regions in Northeast India, typically inhabiting mid-elevation forests.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Leptobrachium rakhinense* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, metallic "peep" notes emitted from rocky streams in forested habitats.
